newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: TRADE DEFICIT IN JAN-APRIL 2.338 BLN LITAS.
newsitem.headline: TRADE DEFICIT IN JAN-APRIL 2.338 BLN LITAS.

text.p: Lithuania's statistics department said on Wednesday that the country's preliminary foreign trade deficit in the first four months of the year was 2.338 billion litas.
The department said in a statement that total exports stood at 4.518 billion litas during the first four months of the year, an 11 percent increase compared to the same period in 1996.
Miports amounted to 6.856 billion litas in January - April of 1997, an increase of 25.6 percent compared to the same period last year, the statement said.
The statement also said that the country's trade deficit in April was 800.4 million litas when exports reached 1.19 billion litas and imports 1.991 billion litas.
The department said on Tuesday that the revised foreign trade deficit for 1996 was 4.8 billion litas.
The major country's trading partners in the first four months of the year were Russia, which accounted for 23.6 percent of exports 26.5 percent of imports.
Germany was second, accounting for 12.2 percent of the country's exports and 16.9 percent of its imports, followed by Belarus at 11.2 percent and 1.8 percent respectively.
The department said that in the first four months of the year 45.9 percent of total exports went to CIS countries and 34.6 percent to European Union countries.
European Union countries accounted for 43.2 percent of total imports and CIS countries for 31.6 percent, the statement said.
